perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He knows Patricia Ndiaye as a colleague at the community bank, where he occasionally helps with maintenance and repairs of bank equipment. They have a friendly, professional relationship.
- He observed Patricia seeming more withdrawn/down than usual. He remembered her as normally vibrant and suspected something was troubling her.
- He asked Patricia if everything was okay. Patricia told him it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked him for asking.
- He told Patricia he understood and was available if she wanted to talk. Patricia said she appreciated it and that it meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments. This deepened his concern.
- He offered to discuss financial planning strategies and budgeting tips with her. Patricia told him that could be helpful because she had been overwhelmed with bills lately, and said she would take him up on it soon.
- He later worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances. He checked with Patricia. She told him he was not prying and that she was grateful for his offer.
- He told her he respected her privacy and only wanted to support her as a friend. She said she appreciated having someone to turn to.
- He formed the impression that Patricia appreciated his concern but preferred to handle her issues privately.
- He continued checking in with Patricia at work. He asked about her weekend; she said she was all good and planned a quiet weekend at home. He said he would probably read and relax, and reminded her he was available if she needed anything.
- Patricia told him she was busy but handling things, thanked him for checking in, said she would keep him in mind, and told him his support was great. Jose replied that he was there anytime and that everyone helps each other out.
- He does not have explicit knowledge of the specific details of Patricia’s personal problems or financial situation beyond what she told him or what he overheard.
